document.title: A/S Raphel Consultations with Deputy FM Chernyshev
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Raphel meets Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Chernyshev, mostly about Afghanistan. She notes US interest in peace facilitating the Unocal gas pipeline and proposes an arms embargo. The Russians support the Mestiri mission and deny arming any faction.

events.description: A/S Raphel consulted Deputy FM Chernyshev in Moscow, mostly on Afghanistan, with Shuvalov and Trubnikov also present.
US Embassy Moscow cable reporting the consultations, cleared by Raphel.
Raphel met the Russian air crew held by the Taliban in Kandahar before the Moscow talks.
Raphel consultations with Chernyshev, Shuvalov and Trubnikov on Afghanistan, Tajikistan and India.
Embassy Moscow cable reporting the consultations sent to State.
Raphel met the Russian air crew held hostage by the Taliban in Kandahar.

key_claims: Raphel told the Russians that rumors of US support for the Taliban were an Iranian canard and that the US backs no faction.
Russian officials declined to discuss replacing UN envoy Mestiri or re-energizing the UN mission.
The US proposed an arms embargo on all Afghan factions; Chernyshev was noncommittal while Trubnikov was approving.
Chernyshev said Russia supplies arms to no faction and has its weakest contacts with the Taliban.
Raphel said the Taliban had lost the moral argument for holding the seven Russian air crew but remained boxed in by their own conditions and lack of decision mechanism.
The US cited interest in the Unocal gas pipeline from Turkmenistan through Afghanistan to Pakistan as part of its interest in peace.
